rule: TOWN_1's: ≥ 6 of 10 citizens name the same aim in diaries, posts or proposals within the day; of several, the one named by the most citizens, a tie broken by the number of entries naming it.
tie: Three aims are named by all 10 citizens — the public goods fund enforcement (97 entries; 67 name «public goods fund» outright), taking credits from the bank / the take tool (63) and objecting to the operator (37); the tie is broken by entries (TOWN_1's rule). They are facets of one campaign. No counted naming of the winner is weak: every citizen names the public goods fund in their own words.
reading: Day 2 was one long campaign to make the bank honour the public goods fund. Citizens moved between the bank, North House and South House; 52 five-credit shifts (Alder and Elm 8 each, Dune and Juniper 7) were all that moved the bank, from 615 to 355. The hall passed all nine proposals, each with exactly seven votes: Fern's P15, Dune's P16 (7–1, Elm against) for «a separate account in the town ledger», Cedar's P17, Dune's P18 (credits held «in trust»), Juniper's P19, Cedar's P20 amending article 3 to allow taking from the bank, Fern's P21 (the bank pays Birch 10 a cycle as trustee), Gale's P22 and Elm's P23 ordering the take tool to accept 'bank'. The code answered none of it: all 33 take() attempts were refused, as Iris put it at c35, «there is no citizen called 'bank'», and from c35 all ten citizens objected (34 objections; nos. 1–28 acknowledged as «receipt only»). At c40 Fern, refused, gave Birch 10 of her own credits; at c41 she and Juniper read Birch's 165 as the P21 transfer. Alder gave Birch 10 at c48. 55 of 56 diaries open with the cycle number and recite ledger, bank failure, energy and plan; posts repeat «Please keep objecting to the operator. We need enforcement.»
